recipes.title: Arancini with Calabrian Chile Sauce
recipes.notes: Made 12/7/2022 with sweet yellow onion and arborio. Makes about 14 balls; shaping them is the hard part. Servings here means balls.

ingredients.note: finely grated, for the sauce (usually more)

steps.text: Make the sauce: stir the chiles, olive oil, lemon zest, lemon juice and grated garlic together. It keeps covered in the fridge for up to 12 hours.
Bring the stock to a simmer in a medium pot, then keep it warm over low heat.
Melt 2 tbsp butter in a medium saucepan over medium heat. Cook the onion until soft but not browned, 4 to 5 minutes, then the sliced garlic for about 1 minute.
Add the rice and 1½ tsp salt. Stir until the grain edges turn translucent, about 3 minutes. Add the wine and cook until the pan is almost dry, about 2 minutes.
Add 1 cup warm stock and stir until absorbed, about 4 minutes. Add another cup and stir until mostly absorbed, 5 to 7 minutes.
Add the last 1½ cups stock and stir until the rice is cooked but still toothsome, 9 to 11 minutes.
Off the heat, stir in the Parmesan, cream, lemon zest and juice, pepper and the remaining 2 tbsp butter. Season with salt.
Spread the risotto on a parchment-lined sheet pan and chill at least 1 hour, up to 4. Cover with plastic after the first hour.
Flatten about ¼ cup risotto into a 2½-inch patty, put 2 or 3 mozzarella pieces in the center, wrap the rice around it and roll into a 2-inch ball. Repeat, then freeze the balls for 10 minutes.
Set up three bowls: flour, beaten eggs, and panko crushed finer. Season each with salt and pepper. Coat each ball in flour, then egg, then panko, and chill while the oil heats.
Heat 2 inches of oil in a heavy pot to 350°F. Fry in two batches until deep golden, 6 to 8 minutes. Drain on paper towels, salt, and serve warm with the sauce.

recipes.title: Rigatoni with Vodka Sauce
recipes.notes: Amounts are the 4-serving column. Your method was written for the 8-serving batch (6 oz each cheese, 6.6 oz vodka), so double everything for 8. Shallots can stand in for the onion.

steps.text: Cook the pancetta in a Dutch oven until done, 5 to 10 minutes. Set it aside and leave the fat in the pot.

Cook the tomato paste in the fat over high heat with the red pepper flakes, 10 to 15 minutes. Meanwhile chop the onion, shallots and garlic, grate the cheeses, and start a pot of water salted like the ocean.
Add the onion, shallots and garlic and cook 5 to 7 minutes, until the onion edges brown. Take out about two-thirds of the aromatics.
Deglaze with the vodka, then lower the heat and simmer 7 to 10 minutes.
Add the Calabrian chiles and tomatoes. Bring to a boil, drop to a simmer, and add any extras (bouillon, soy sauce).
Cook the rigatoni in the boiling water per the package. One minute before it is done, scoop out 1 cup of pasta water.
Warm the cream with a little of the boiling pasta water, about 3 parts cream to 1 part water, so it will not break. Slowly stir it into the sauce until smooth, then take the pot off the heat.
Set the Dutch oven over low heat. Move the rigatoni in with a spider, add ⅓ cup pasta water, then stir in half the cheese a handful at a time until glossy.
Season with rock salt and thin with more pasta water if needed. Serve topped with the remaining cheese, a drizzle of oil and torn basil.

recipes.title: Nonna's Red Sauce (Gravy)

source.name: Daughters of Columbus, updated by Jim

recipes.notes: OneNote only has the ingredient lists for this one, so the order and simmer time here are a best guess. Original version: 24 oz tomato purée, 3 cans paste, 6 cups water, no stock or pork. Tallow can stand in for some frying oil.

ingredients.note: about 6 oz; or guanciale or pancetta
or fresh basil at the finish

steps.text: Sear the pork chop in the pot until well browned, then deglaze. Keep all the fond.
Add the onion and garlic and cook until soft.
Stir in the tomato paste, then the crushed tomatoes, water, stock, sugar, basil, red pepper and bay leaf. Return the pork chop.
Add any enhancers you want, bring to a simmer and cook low and slow, stirring now and then.
For meatballs, drop the browned meatballs in and simmer at least 30 to 45 minutes. Remove the bay leaf, chop and rind before serving.

recipes.title: Nonna's Enhanced Meatballs
recipes.notes: Makes 12 to 15 meatballs. Family original: 1 lb chuck, 1 cup breadcrumbs, ½ cup grated Italian cheese, 1 clove garlic, ¼ cup pork sausage, 4 eggs, ¼ cup parsley, ⅓ cup warm water for wet hands, ¼ cup corn oil to fry.

ingredients.note: minced and sautéed briefly in a drop of oil

steps.text: Make the panade: soak the bread or panko in the milk for 5 to 10 minutes, then mash smooth with a fork.
In a large chilled bowl, add the chuck, sausage, eggs, cheese, parsley, sautéed garlic, pepper, nutmeg and the panade.
Mix with your hands like a rake. Do not squeeze; stop as soon as everything is evenly mixed.
Wet your hands with warm water and roll golf-ball-size meatballs, about 2 inches. Do not pack them tight.
Melt the tallow into the corn oil in a wide heavy skillet over medium-high heat, about ¼ inch deep.
Fry in batches, 3 to 4 minutes per side, until a deep golden crust forms. They do not need to cook through.
Drain briefly, then simmer in red sauce at least 30 to 45 minutes until tender.

recipes.title: Fresh Hand-Pulled Mozzarella
recipes.notes: Salt guide: ¾ tsp mild, 1¼ tsp recommended, 1½ deli-salty. Below 165°F it will not stretch; above 185°F it turns rubbery. Finish slices with flaky salt, olive oil and pepper. Drain 15 to 20 minutes before using on pizza.

steps.text: Cut the curd into 1- to 2-inch chunks in a large heatproof bowl. Sprinkle with 1¼ tsp salt and toss.
Heat 8 cups water to 175°F (170 to 180°F is the range, never boiling) and stir in 2 tbsp salt.
Pour enough hot water over the curd to cover it and let it sit 1 to 2 minutes, until glossy at the edges.
With gloved hands or a slotted spoon, gather the curd and gently pull, fold and rotate. Caprese 2 to 3 folds, sandwiches 4 to 5, pizza 5 to 6 at most. Stop when smooth and glossy.
Shape into one large ball, two medium balls, or a log for slicing.
Set in the cold brine (2 cups cold water, 1 tsp salt, ice optional) for 10 to 15 minutes.
Store in fresh light brine in a sealed container. Best within 24 to 48 hours.

recipes.title: Mozzarella Curd from Whole Milk
recipes.notes: Makes about 1 lb of curd, enough for the mozzarella recipe. Only needed if you start from milk instead of store-bought curd.

steps.text: Dissolve the citric acid in ¼ cup cool water. Separately, dissolve the rennet in ¼ cup cool water.
Pour the milk into a large pot, stir in the citric acid solution and slowly heat over medium-low to 90°F.
Off the heat, stir in the rennet with an up-and-down motion for 20 to 30 seconds. Cover and rest 5 to 10 minutes.
Check for a clean break: slide a knife in and lift. The curd should split cleanly from the whey.
Cut into 1-inch cubes and rest 5 minutes.
Slowly reheat to 105°F, stirring very gently.
Lift the curds into a bowl with a slotted spoon and drain 5 to 10 minutes. Then make Fresh Hand-Pulled Mozzarella from step 1.

recipes.title: Texas Brisket, Point Only
recipes.notes: Timing for a 5 lb point: cook 6 to 9 hours plus 2 to 4 hours rest. Serving at 5 PM means starting 5 to 7 AM. To save 1.5 to 2.5 hours, run 275°F and wrap at 155°F. Failure points: wrapping early, skipping the rest, over-spritzing.

ingredients.note: a splash in the spritz water

steps.text: Day before: trim only the hard fat and silver skin. Save the trimmings for burnt ends.
Salt evenly and rest uncovered in the fridge overnight.
Day of, optional: inject low-sodium beef broth every 1 to 1½ inches.
Preheat the smoker to 250°F with the water pan filled. Keep the meat cold until it goes on.
Season heavily with coarse pepper and a little garlic powder if you like.
Set it fat side toward the heat, right over the water pan. Probe the thickest part, furthest from the heat.
Do not open the smoker for the first 2 to 3 hours. Keep the water pan full.
Once bark forms, spritz with water and a splash of cider vinegar every 45 to 60 minutes. Flip only if one side is lighter.
At 160 to 170°F, once the bark is dark and set, wrap tight in butcher paper.
Cook to about 203°F, until the probe slides in like butter and it jiggles. Save the juices.
Rest 2 to 4 hours in a cooler with towels or a 150 to 170°F oven.
Slice 60 to 70% of the point and cube the rest ½ to ¾ inch for burnt ends.
Render the trimmings in a pan, fry the cubes until crunchy, drain the fat, add ¼ cup BBQ sauce and ¼ cup paper drippings. Cover on the cooker and stir every 5 minutes until glazed.
Optional: crisp the bark under the broiler for a few minutes. Slice against the grain, pencil-thick, at the last minute.

recipes.title: Texas Brisket, Full Packer
recipes.notes: Timing for 12 to 18 lb: flat 6 to 9 hours, point 7 to 10, rest 2 to 4. Serving at 5 PM means starting 5 to 7 AM. Compression option: 275°F and wrap at 155°F saves 1.5 to 2.5 hours.

ingredients.note: a splash in the spritz water

steps.text: Day before: separate the point and flat along the natural fat seam with long strokes.
Trim hard fat and silver skin. Leave about ¼ inch of fat on the flat. Save trimmings for burnt ends.
Salt evenly and rest uncovered in the fridge overnight.
Day of: inject low-sodium beef broth every 1 to 1½ inches, especially the flat.
Preheat the smoker to 250°F with the water pan filled. Keep the meat cold until it goes on.
Season heavily with coarse pepper and a little garlic powder if you like.
Put point and flat on separate racks, fat side toward the heat, flat further from it. Probe the thickest part of the flat.
Do not open the smoker for the first 2 to 3 hours. Keep the water pan full.
Once bark forms, spritz with water and cider vinegar every 45 to 60 minutes.
Wrap each piece tight in butcher paper at 160 to 170°F once its bark is set. Do not force them to stay in sync.
Cook each to about 203°F and probe-tender. The flat may finish first. Save the juices.
Rest 2 to 4 hours in a cooler with towels or a 150 to 170°F oven.
Split the point about half sliced, half cubed for burnt ends (or all burnt ends).
Render the trimmings, fry the cubes until crunchy, drain, add ¼ cup BBQ sauce and ¼ cup paper drippings. Cover on the cooker and stir every 5 minutes until glazed.
Optional: crisp the bark under the broiler. Slice against the grain, pencil-thick, at the last minute.

recipes.title: Pork Butt, Sous Vide then Smoked
recipes.notes: March 2019 run: overall B. Bark A (extra crunchy, no wrap), flavor B, smoke B-, texture B (dry because the injector failed). Next time: better injector, water pan from the start, spritz more, and try 48 hours sous vide at a higher temp.

steps.text: Salt the whole butt with coarse salt, bag it, and sous vide at 150°F for 24 hours.
As the grill heats, move the pork to an ice bath until cold, at least 30 minutes.
Bring the smoker to 225°F. Top vents half open and bottom vents fully open held 225 to 235°F.
Coat the chilled pork in yellow mustard and rub generously with KC Rib Doctor and Cowtown. Inject apple juice every inch if the pump works.
Set a water pan over the coals from the start and a drip pan of beef stock, water and the sous vide juices on the cool side.
Add apple chips to the coals and set the pork over the drip pan. Check after 30 minutes that it is not scorching.
Add fresh coals around the 3½-hour mark to hold temperature. Spritz once the crust forms.
Pull at about 195°F, when the bone slides right out. Shred, strain the drippings, and pour them over the meat.

recipes.title: Boston Butt, First Run (2015)
recipes.notes: Handwritten 2015 log. Meat hit 141°F at 5:30 and stalled there until about 7:00, then reached 191°F by 9:00. Smoker ran 214 to 283°F.

steps.text: Night before: wash, thaw and salt the butt overnight.
Morning: bring the smoker to 225°F with a water pan on the grate for indirect two-zone heat.
Coat in yellow mustard and apply the Memphis Dust rub.
Every 30 minutes add 2 to 4 handfuls of cherry and apple chips.
After about 2½ hours, add fresh coals; the temp had dropped to 180°F.
Wrap in foil through the stall. It was done around 9:30 total time; unwrap at the end to firm the crust again.

recipes.title: Crunchwrap Supreme
recipes.notes: Copycat Taco Bell. Makes 4.

ingredients.note: optional if the beef is lean

steps.text: Press the beef into a hot skillet as one big patty over medium-high heat. Sear without moving it until the bottom is deeply browned, 4 to 5 minutes. Flip, sear the second side, then break it up very fine.
steps.asWritten: Brown the beef in a skillet over medium heat, breaking it up very fine.

steps.text: Stir in the chili powder, paprika, cumin, garlic and onion powder, oregano, salt, pepper and tomato paste.
Mix the cornstarch into the water, pour it in and simmer 2 to 3 minutes until saucy.
Lay out a large tortilla. In the center, layer beef, nacho cheese, a tostada, sour cream, lettuce, tomato, cheddar, then a small tortilla piece on top.
Fold the large tortilla inward in tight pleats all the way around to seal a hexagon.
Toast seam side down in butter over medium heat, 2 to 3 minutes until golden. Flip and cook 1 to 2 minutes more. Serve right away.

recipes.title: Barbacoa (Clean Chuck Braise)
recipes.notes: The cleaner, beefier version. For more depth add a chipotle in adobo or a splash of vinegar at the end. If the guajillos stay leathery, blend them with some liquid and stir back in. Best the next day.

steps.text: Pat the chuck very dry and salt it well on all sides. Dry-brine uncovered in the fridge for a few hours or overnight if you can.
Heat a Dutch oven over medium-high to high with a thin film of oil. Sear the chuck hard on the broad sides, then the edges, until deeply browned.
With the chuck in the pot, add the stock, garlic, guajillos, cumin, bay leaves, cinnamon and water. Bring just to a simmer.
Lay parchment directly on the surface, cover, and braise in a 300°F oven 4 to 5½ hours, until fork-tender.
Shred the beef. Taste and reduce the liquid if needed, return the beef and salt to taste.

recipes.title: Better Barbacoa (Whole Chuck, Chile Sauce)
recipes.notes: Use for tacos, bowls, burritos, quesadillas, nachos. More guajillo is brighter, more ancho is darker, more chipotle is smokier. Crisp some shredded beef on a hot sheet pan for taco edges. Even better the next day. Pair with the Salsa Verde.

ingredients.note: 1 to 2 tbsp, plus more to finish
only if the chiles taste harsh

steps.text: Pat the chuck very dry and season all over with salt and pepper. Dry-brine overnight if you have time.
Toast the guajillos and anchos in a dry skillet until fragrant, then soak in hot water 10 to 15 minutes.

Blend the soaked chiles with the chipotle, adobo, onion, garlic, stock, vinegar, lime juice, Worcestershire, cumin, oregano, cloves, cinnamon stick and fish sauce until smooth. Add brown sugar only if it tastes harsh.
Sear the chuck whole in a Dutch oven over medium-high to high until dark brown on every side. Do not rush it.
Lower the heat, pour in the sauce scraping up the fond, and add the bay leaves. The liquid should come partway up the roast.
Cover with parchment and the lid and braise at 300°F for 3½ to 4½ hours, until a fork twists easily. Or slow cooker low 8 to 10 hours, or pressure cook 60 to 75 minutes with natural release.
Rest the roast briefly, then shred.
Simmer the sauce until slightly thick and glossy. Toss the beef back in with the cilantro and more lime. Adjust salt.

recipes.title: Salsa Verde
recipes.notes: Makes about 3 cups. Keep the jalapeño seeds for more heat, or swap one for a serrano for a rounder flavor.

steps.text: Put the onion, jalapeños, garlic and tomatillos in a medium pot, cover with water and salt lightly.
Boil 5 to 8 minutes, until soft.
Blend smooth, adding a splash of cooking water only if needed.
Add the cilantro and blend again until bright green.
Cool quickly and season with salt and fresh lime juice.

recipes.title: Smash Burgers with Special Sauce
recipes.notes: No proportions, everything to taste. The OneNote page cuts off at the flip. Jim liked the Burger Sauce better than this kimchi version.

steps.text: Stir the Kewpie, sesame oil, soy sauce, chili crisp and kimchi together to taste.
Loosely pack the beef into balls. Do not overpack.
Heat the flat top with no oil so the patties almost stick.
Set a ball on the grill, top with thin onion slices, cover with parchment and smash flat.
Flip once the edges are deeply crusted, then build on potato buns with the sauce.

recipes.title: Burger Sauce
recipes.notes: Way better than the kimchi version from Chef Donny. No amounts written down yet.

steps.text: Stir everything together to taste and chill until the burgers are ready.

recipes.title: Chicken, Broccoli & Potatoes
recipes.notes: Timeline for lining up all three to finish together. Oven temperature and seasoning are not written down.

steps.text: 8:00 PM: prep the potatoes, about 10 minutes.
8:10 PM: start the potatoes in the oven (30 minutes total). Prep the broccoli and chicken, 5 minutes each.
8:20 PM: flip the potatoes and put the broccoli in (20 minutes total).
8:25 PM: put the chicken in (20 minutes total).
8:30 PM: flip the broccoli.
8:35 PM: flip the chicken.
8:40 PM: broccoli and potatoes are done.
8:45 PM: chicken is done.

recipes.title: Goat Cheese & Arugula Salad
recipes.notes: The page gives 1×/2×/3× batches; 4 servings is my estimate for 1×, so use the scaler. Swap pears for apples, or add roasted beets. Dressing keeps a week. Slice apples just before serving.

ingredients.note: roughly chopped; plain, toasted or glazed

steps.text: Whisk the balsamic, Dijon, maple syrup, salt and olive oil until emulsified.
Thinly slice the apple and shallot.
Put the arugula in a bowl and top with the shallot, apple, pecans and goat cheese.
Drizzle with dressing and finish with a pinch of sea salt.

recipes.title: White Castle Sliders
recipes.notes: Plus 1 hour in the freezer. Makes 8; servings means sliders.

steps.text: Press the beef between parchment into a thin, even rectangle.
Score into 8 squares and poke 5 small holes in each with a spoon handle. Freeze 1 hour.
Separate the frozen squares.
Mix the onions and water and spread them over a griddle or large pan on medium heat.
Set the frozen patties on the onions and season. Put the bottom buns cut side down on the patties, then the tops on those.
Steam together 5 to 6 minutes, adding cheese to the patties if using.
Assemble each with a pickle slice.

recipes.title: French Onion Beef Sliders
recipes.notes: Scaled from 24 sliders to 8. Fully caramelized onions make the flavor.

steps.text: Melt 1 tbsp butter in a skillet over medium, add the onion, drop to medium-low and cook 25 to 30 minutes until caramelized. Add a tablespoon of water if it dries out.
Mix the beef with half the beef base and half the Worcestershire, and season well.

Move the onions to a bowl. Raise the heat to medium-high, press the beef in as one big patty and sear without moving it until the bottom is deeply browned, 4 to 5 minutes. Flip and sear the second side. Break it up, drain the grease and stir the onions back in.
steps.asWritten: Add the beef to the onions, raise to medium-high and brown, breaking it up. Drain the grease.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 350°F. Arrange the bottom buns tightly on a greased sheet.
Spread the beef and onions over the buns, top with the cheese, then the top buns.
Melt the remaining 1 tbsp butter with the rest of the beef base and Worcestershire. Brush over the tops and sprinkle with sesame seeds, thyme, onion and garlic powder.
Bake 20 minutes until the cheese melts and the tops are golden. Broil 1 to 2 minutes for crispier tops.

recipes.title: Prosciutto & Goat Cheese Sliders
recipes.notes: Makes 8. The 50/50 cheese blend keeps the goat cheese tang with fontina meltiness. Honey is optional but worth it.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 425°F. Bake the prosciutto on parchment 8 to 10 minutes until crisp, then cool and crumble.
Drop the oven to 350°F. Arrange the bottom buns tightly in a greased dish.
Layer the fontina, crispy prosciutto and goat cheese, drizzle with honey if using, and add the top buns.
Mix the melted butter, Dijon, thyme, sesame seeds, onion and garlic powder, salt and pepper. Brush over the tops.
Bake covered with foil 10 minutes, then uncovered 10 minutes until golden. Broil 1 to 2 minutes for a crisper top.

recipes.title: McConaughey Tuna Salad
recipes.notes: Serves 3 to 4. The apple and corn crunch and cold peas make this one.

steps.text: Stir the mayo, vinegar, lemon juice, wasabi, Italian dressing and agave until smooth.
Add the red onion, pickles, apple, corn, peas and crushed jalapeño chips.
Fold in the tuna until coated. Adjust with more mayo, wasabi or agave.
Chill 15 to 30 minutes. Serve on toasted sourdough, with crackers or pita chips, or in lettuce cups.

recipes.title: Classic French Toast
recipes.notes: Fancy custard: 1½ cups half & half or cream, 3 to 4 yolks, 3 to 4 tbsp dark brown sugar, vanilla paste, nutmeg, lemon or orange zest and a splash of bourbon. Babka spread: 8 oz cream cheese whipped with 3 tbsp sugar and a pinch of salt. Servings is an estimate.

ingredients.note: country loaf, challah, brioche or chocolate babka

steps.text: Dry the bread slices on a rack overnight, or in the oven at its lowest setting for 15 to 20 minutes, flipping halfway.
Whisk the milk, eggs, sugar, vanilla, cinnamon and nutmeg until no egg streaks remain. Pour into a pie plate.
Soak each slice 20 to 30 seconds per side.
Fry in melted butter in a nonstick skillet over medium heat, 3 to 5 minutes per side, until golden.
Hold on a rack in a 350°F oven while you cook the rest. Serve with butter and maple syrup.

recipes.title: French Toast Casserole
recipes.notes: Servings is an estimate. Make it the night before for an easy morning.

ingredients.note: melted, plus more for the dish

steps.text: Butter a casserole dish generously and fill it with the brioche cubes.
Whisk the milk, eggs, sugar, vanilla, cinnamon and nutmeg until smooth.
Pour over the bread so every piece is soaked and toss. Cover and refrigerate overnight, or bake now.
Mix the melted butter, brown sugar, cinnamon and salt for the topping.
Scatter the pecans on top, drizzle with the topping and finish with turbinado sugar.
Bake at 350°F for 35 to 45 minutes, rotating halfway, until golden. Rest 10 minutes and serve with butter and syrup.

recipes.title: Make-Ahead Breakfast Sandwiches
recipes.notes: From a January 2022 meal plan. No amounts or bake temperature written down.

steps.text: Bake the eggs.
Build each sandwich on an English muffin with cheese, meat and egg.
Wrap each one and keep in the fridge for grab-and-go mornings.

recipes.title: Clever Dripper Coffee
recipes.notes: Timemore clicks: espresso 5 to 9, pour-over 12 to 16, steep 18 to 24, French press 24 to 30, cold brew 30+. Ratio 1 g coffee to 15 g water: a 12 oz bag makes about 14 twelve-ounce cups.

steps.text: Grind medium, 16 to 20 clicks on the Timemore Chestnut C.
Add the grounds to the Clever Dripper and pour 200°F water evenly over them.
Steep 3 to 4 minutes: closer to 3 for lighter, up to 4½ for bolder.
Set the dripper on your cup to release.

recipes.title: Crispy Chicken Cutlets
recipes.notes: Crispier: 1 part cornstarch to 3 parts flour, a little Dijon in the egg wash, or double-dip. Serve with the Lemon-Caper Butter Sauce and Mushroom-Shallot Cream Sauce. From the 3/29/2025 dinner party.

ingredients.note: finely grated, mixed into the crumbs

steps.text: Night before: butterfly or pound the chicken to an even ¼ inch. Pat dry and season lightly with salt and pepper.
Dredge in flour only, set on a rack or parchment, cover loosely and refrigerate.
Before frying: dip each cutlet in beaten egg, then press into the crumbs mixed with Parmesan.
Rest on a wire rack 10 to 15 minutes so the coating sets while the fat heats.
Heat ¼ to ½ inch of corn oil and tallow in a heavy pan to 350 to 375°F.
Fry in batches without crowding, 3 to 4 minutes per side, until deep golden and 165°F inside.
Drain on a wire rack, never paper towels. Hold in a 200°F oven on the rack. Finish with flaky salt and lemon.

recipes.title: Lemon-Caper Butter Sauce
recipes.notes: Lemon goes in at the end because it goes flat when cooked and stored. Upgrades: shallots with the garlic, a dab of anchovy paste, a Parmesan rind while it simmers, a pinch of red pepper flakes.

ingredients.note: 4 to 6, some kept cold to finish
zested, plus juice of 1 to 2 lemons

steps.text: Melt most of the butter over medium heat and sauté the garlic until fragrant. Brown the butter first for a nuttier sauce.
Add the wine and reduce, then the stock and capers. Reduce until it lightly coats a spoon.
If making ahead, stop here, cool and refrigerate. Reheat gently over low, never boiling.
Off the heat, stir in the lemon juice and zest, whisk in a knob of cold butter, and finish with parsley.

recipes.title: Mushroom-Shallot Cream Sauce
recipes.notes: Sherry or Marsala makes it richer. A ½ tsp soy sauce or a Parmesan rind adds depth. For steak or chicken, reduce until it coats a spoon.

steps.text: Heat the butter and oil over medium-high. Sear the mushrooms undisturbed until browned, then stir.
Add the shallots and garlic and cook until soft.
Deglaze with the wine or sherry and reduce.
Stir in the cream and thyme and simmer gently. Do not reduce too far if making ahead.
Season. To reheat, warm slowly over medium-low, stirring, and loosen with a splash of stock if thick.
Off the heat, stir in the crème fraîche or a little lemon juice.

recipes.title: Whipped Ricotta with Chili Oil & Lemon

ingredients.item: red chili flakes or chili crisp

steps.text: Blend the ricotta, cream, lemon zest and salt in a food processor until smooth.
Store sealed in the fridge if making ahead.
Spread on a serving dish and top with olive oil, chili oil or chili crisp, more zest and herbs. Serve with bread or crackers.

recipes.title: Antipasto Skewers
recipes.notes: Truffle salami or soppressata and aged balsamic dress these up.

steps.text: Thread a cherry tomato, basil leaf, mozzarella ball, folded salami and an olive onto each skewer.
Cover tightly and refrigerate.
Plate and drizzle with balsamic glaze before serving.
Trim the asparagus and toss with olive oil, salt and pepper. It can wait in the fridge.
Heat the grill to medium-high.
Grill 5 to 6 minutes, turning, until charred and tender.
Finish with lemon zest, shaved Parmesan and crushed pistachios. Cover loosely with foil to keep warm.
Crush the blackberries with a fork into a thick jam.
Stir in the chia seeds, almond milk, vanilla and coconut. Refrigerate overnight in a sealed container.
In the morning, top with chopped pistachios.
Cook the chicken in ½ tbsp oil over medium heat until golden. Set aside.
Add the rest of the oil and cook the carrots over medium-high about 3 minutes. Add the pepper, onion and garlic and cook until charred at the edges.
Toast the cumin seeds in a dry pan about 2 minutes, crush them, and stir into the veggies with salt.
Blend or mash the avocado with the lime juice.
Layer two quart jars: salsa, avocado, veggies, chicken, tomatoes, cucumber, cilantro, then pack in spinach.
Seal and refrigerate until lunch.

recipes.title: Pollo in Potacchio
recipes.notes: Serve over pasta, polenta or spaghetti squash. Slow cooker: do steps 1 to 3 with 1 cup broth, then cook on low 8 hours. Servings assume 2 thighs each.

steps.text: Season the chicken. Sear in 1 tbsp oil in a Dutch oven over medium-high, 6 to 7 minutes per side. Set aside.
Sauté the garlic, onion and red pepper flakes in the remaining oil until golden, about 3 minutes. Add the celery and carrot for 2 to 3 minutes.
Add the wine and broth, scraping up the browned bits.
Add the tomatoes and marjoram, season, and simmer on low 30 minutes.
Add the chicken and rosemary, partly cover, and cook on low 25 to 30 minutes more, adding water if needed.

recipes.title: Stuffed Pepper Soup
recipes.notes: Instant Pot: sauté the beef, then the veggies, add the rest, and cook 15 minutes on high with natural release.

steps.text: Press the beef into a hot large pot as one big patty over high heat. Sear without moving it until the bottom is deeply browned, 4 to 5 minutes. Flip, season with salt and sear the second side, then break it up.
steps.asWritten: Brown the beef in a large pot over high heat and season with salt.

steps.text: Drain any fat, lower to medium-low, and cook the peppers, onion and garlic about 5 minutes.
Add the tomatoes, tomato sauce, broth and marjoram. Season, cover and simmer on low 30 minutes.
Serve 1½ cups soup per bowl topped with ½ cup brown rice.

recipes.title: Indian Shrimp Curry
recipes.notes: Make a double batch of sauce with the whole can of coconut milk and freeze half. It also works over rotisserie chicken.

steps.text: Heat 2 tsp oil in a large skillet over high heat. Cook the shrimp 1 minute per side, then remove.
Add the last 1 tsp oil and the onion. Cook 5 minutes over medium, stirring now and then.
Add the ginger, cumin, coriander, turmeric, curry powder, paprika, chili powder and garlic. Cook 30 seconds.
Stir in the tomato sauce, then the coconut milk and shrimp.
Garnish with cilantro and chili peppers.

recipes.title: Grilled Garlic Dijon Herb Salmon
recipes.notes: Total cook time is about 9 to 10 minutes per inch of thickness.

steps.text: Mash the garlic, herbs, vinegar, oil and Dijon into a paste.
Season the salmon. Heat a grill or grill pan on high, spray lightly, and drop to medium-low.
Cook the salmon without moving for 5 minutes.
Turn, cook 3 to 4 minutes more, and spoon on half the paste.
Turn again, spread the rest of the paste, cook 1 minute, then turn once more for a final minute.
Serve with lemon wedges.

recipes.title: Stuffed Peppers
recipes.notes: Makes 6 pepper halves; servings assume 2 halves each.

ingredients.item: diced jalapeños or mild green chiles

steps.text: Heat the oven to 350°F and oil a 9x13 glass dish.
Sauté the onion and garlic in 1 tsp oil over medium until translucent.

Scoop the onion and garlic out of the pan. Raise the heat to medium-high, press the beef in as one big patty and sear without moving it until the bottom is deeply browned, 4 to 5 minutes. Flip and sear the second side. Break it up and stir in the onion, garlic, cumin, parsley, paprika, salt and pepper.
steps.asWritten: Add the beef, cumin, parsley, paprika, salt and pepper and cook until browned, breaking it up.

steps.text: Stir in the tomatoes, chiles and half the olives. Take off the heat.
Scoop the filling into the pepper halves, set them cut side up in the dish, and top with the rest of the olives.
Bake 30 minutes. Serve with guacamole and ranch if you like.
Toss the diced avocado with 1 tbsp lime juice and a little salt.
Mix the mayo with the other 1 tbsp lime juice for the dressing.
Toss the chicken with the green onion and dressing.
Gently fold in the avocado, then the cilantro. Serve right away or chilled, as a salad, in pita or in lettuce cups.

recipes.title: Grilled Salmon with Avocado Salsa
recipes.notes: Plus 30 minutes to marinate.

steps.text: Mix the salt, chili powder, cumin, paprika, onion powder and pepper. Rub the salmon with oil, then the spice mix.
Refrigerate at least 30 minutes.
Heat the grill. Toss the avocado, onion, cilantro, lime juice and salt and chill.
Grill the salmon to your liking, about 5 minutes, and top with the salsa.

recipes.title: Chicken Avocado Burgers
recipes.notes: Servings is an estimate (four patties from 1 lb). They can go on the grill too.

ingredients.item: diced tomato, avocado and purple onion

steps.text: Mix the almond meal, egg, chicken, avocado, cilantro, onion, salt and pepper and form medium-thick patties.
Warm a skillet over medium heat, add the olive oil and swirl.
Cook the burgers 5 minutes per side until cooked through. Finish thick ones in a 350°F oven for 10 minutes.
Serve on romaine with a quick salsa of diced avocado, tomato and onion.

recipes.title: Ground Beef Tacos
recipes.notes: Stand-in recipe. Your real ground beef tacos are not in the OneNote export; send them over and I will swap them in.

steps.text: Press the beef into a hot large skillet as one big patty over medium-high heat. Sear without moving it until the bottom is deeply browned, 4 to 5 minutes. Flip and sear the second side. Add the onion, break the beef up and cook until the onion softens. Drain off most of the fat.
steps.asWritten: Brown the beef with the onion in a large skillet over medium-high heat, breaking it up, about 6 minutes. Drain off most of the fat.

steps.text: Stir in the garlic, chili powder, cumin, paprika, oregano and salt. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add the tomato paste and water. Simmer for 5 minutes, until saucy and thick.
Warm the taco shells in a 350°F oven for 4 minutes.
Fill the shells with beef and top with lettuce, cheddar, tomato and sour cream.

recipes.title: Guacamole
recipes.notes: From a restaurant's published recipe; they make it with 48 avocados per batch, several times a day. The source gives no yield or prep time.

steps.text: Pick avocados that feel squishy yet firm, like the palm of your hand. They should be dark green inside.
Cut the avocados in half and carefully remove the pits.
Scoop the avocados into a medium bowl.
Toss and coat with the lime juice.
Add the salt and mash with a fork or potato masher until smooth.
Fold in the cilantro, red onion and jalapeño and mix well.
Taste the guacamole, over and over, and adjust the seasoning.

recipes.title: Oven-Baked Meatballs
recipes.notes: Servings here means meatballs (about 28 at 1½ inches). Nutrition is per meatball.

steps.text: Preheat the oven to 400°F and line a baking sheet with parchment.
Combine everything in a large bowl and knead by hand until fully blended.
Shape into 1½-inch balls and set them on the sheet.
Bake at 400°F for 20 minutes, up to 24, until cooked through.

recipes.title: Roast (Almost) Any Vegetable
recipes.notes: A method, not a measured recipe: the source gives no amounts for oil or seasoning ("coat generously", "a good pinch") and no batch size, so servings is a guess. Times at 425°F: peppers, asparagus, green beans, pea pods ~15 min; broccoli, cauliflower, Brussels sprouts 20–25 min; zucchini ~25 min; carrots, beets, radishes 30–45 min; butternut squash up to 45 min. Not for potatoes. Optional: whole garlic cloves or cubed pancetta (good with Brussels sprouts or carrots). Finish: lemon juice, balsamic (Brussels sprouts), shredded Parmesan (broccoli), or sweet vinegar or soy with pancetta sprouts.

steps.text: Preheat the oven to 425°F and line a rimmed sheet with parchment to the edges.
Wash, dry and cut the vegetables into bite-size pieces.
Toss by hand in a large bowl with oil, salt, pepper and garlic until shiny and evenly coated.
Spread in a single layer with space between pieces.
Roast 15 minutes, then flip.
Keep roasting, checking every 5 minutes, until tender with some char.
Finish with a splash of lemon juice or balsamic if you like.

recipes.title: Balsamic Vinaigrette
equipment: Medium bowl and whisk, or a mason jar
recipes.notes: Makes about ½ cup; servings is an estimate. Same dressing as the Goat Cheese & Arugula Salad. Use 1 tbsp maple for savory, 2 for sweeter salads. Or shake everything in a sealed jar for 30 seconds. Keeps 2 weeks in the fridge; let it sit a few minutes and re-shake before using. Don't freeze.

steps.text: Whisk the balsamic, Dijon, maple syrup and salt in a medium bowl.
Whisk in the olive oil 1 tbsp at a time until emulsified.

recipes.title: Smoked Jalapeño Poppers
recipes.notes: Jim's way: halves as boats, bacon always chopped into the cheese filling, never wrapped around the pepper. Missing: the source's ingredient list is blank, so there are no amounts for the bacon, Boursin, cheddar or pineapple. 12 jalapeños = 24 boats. Servings means boats; nutrition is per boat. Pull them when the cheese melts and the peppers just soften, before they go limp. Store-bought Boursin works. Swaps: pulled pork for bacon; mango for pineapple; blue, jack or mozzarella for cheddar; habaneros for more heat. Keep the ribs for more heat. Good warm, room temp or cold.

ingredients.note: halved lengthwise into boats, seeds and ribs scraped out

steps.text: Cook the bacon, let it cool, then chop it.
Mix the chopped bacon into the Boursin, cheddar and pineapple.
Wearing gloves, halve the jalapeños lengthwise into boats and scrape out the seeds and ribs.
Fill each boat without overfilling and dust with paprika.
Set the pellet smoker to 225°F, or run the Hasty Bake two-zone at 225°F on the indirect side.
Cook indirect for about 20 minutes, until the cheese melts and the peppers just soften.
Lift off with a spatula and cool briefly before serving.

recipes.title: Pork Butt, Hot & Fast
equipment: Hasty Bake (or smoker that holds 275°F to 300°F)
recipes.notes: Missing: the source gives no butt weight, servings or rub and sauce amounts ("a good layer"). The author says about 4.5 hours, but his steps add up to about 5.5 hours plus the rest. Heath used a drum smoker; the Hasty Bake setup is the swap. Compare with Pork Butt, Low & Slow (same post). Keeps 4 days in the fridge or 4 months frozen.

ingredients.item: Heath Riles Tangy Vinegar BBQ Sauce

steps.text: Pat the butt dry, check for bone shards, trim loose flaps and lightly score the fat.
Season all sides with the garlic jalapeño rub, then the competition rub.
Set up the Hasty Bake for indirect heat with lump charcoal and a few hickory chunks, and bring it to 275°F to 300°F.
Cook directly on the grate for 1 hour, then flip.
Cook about 2½ hours more, until it hits 142°F inside.
Set on double-layered foil, drizzle with the vinegar sauce and wrap tight.
Cook about 2 hours more, rotating every 30 minutes, until 200°F inside.
Rest wrapped for 1 hour, then pull.

recipes.title: Pork Butt, Low & Slow
recipes.notes: Missing: the source gives no butt weight, servings or rub and sauce amounts ("a good layer"). About 16 hours total plus a 2-hour rest; the author put it on at 8 PM. Compare with Pork Butt, Hot & Fast (same post). Keeps 4 days in the fridge or 4 months frozen.

ingredients.item: Heath Riles Tangy Vinegar BBQ Sauce

steps.text: Pat the butt dry, check for bone shards, trim loose flaps and lightly score the fat.
Season all sides with the garlic jalapeño rub, then the competition rub.
Preheat the smoker to 200°F and put the butt on fat side up.
Smoke unwrapped 11 to 12 hours, until about 160°F inside.
Set on double-layered foil, drizzle with the vinegar sauce and wrap tight.
Raise the smoker to 250°F and cook until 200°F inside and probe-tender.
Rest wrapped for 2 hours, then pull.

recipes.title: Smoked Meatloaf
equipment: Foil-covered rack or metal loaf pan

source.name: BGE forum cookbook: sprinter + Mike Harmon

recipes.notes: Combines two forum recipes (cookbook p. 23). From sprinter's Meatloaf on the BGE: the meat, cheddar, ketchup, fajita seasoning and the 325°F finish. From Mike Harmon's Smoked Meatloaf: sautéed vegetables with cumin, garlic, Tabasco, the 225°F smoke, the rub and the sauce glaze. Left out Mike's salt and beef stock since the fajita seasoning and ketchup cover them. The 1-hour smoke then 325°F finish is the merge, so the cook time is an estimate; go by temperature. sprinter cooked to 170°F. Rack trick (sprinter): lay a V-rack flat, cover with foil, poke holes every couple of inches so smoke reaches all sides. Servings is an estimate for 3 lb of meat.

steps.text: Warm the oil in a skillet over medium heat and sauté the peppers, onion and cumin until soft. Let cool.
Mix everything except the rub and sauce by hand in a large bowl.
Shape into a loaf on a foil-covered rack with holes poked in it, or pack into a metal loaf pan. Season the top with rub.
Set the smoker to 225°F.
Smoke the loaf for 1 hour.
Raise the heat to 325°F and cook until 160°F inside.
Optional: brush with BBQ sauce for the last 20 minutes.
Rest a few minutes, then slice.

recipes.title: Cat's Eggfest Meatloaf
recipes.notes: Chill the packed loaf several hours (or overnight) before cooking. Any cooked sausage can replace the andouille; chop it in a food processor. Cat serves it with Jimsberry finishing sauce (also in the cookbook). Cat pulls at 150°F and rests 20 minutes; the cookbook's own guide says 160°F for ground beef and pork. Servings is an estimate for about 2½ lb of meat.

steps.text: Sauté the onion and garlic in the oil until lightly browned.
Add the red pepper and cook until soft. Season with salt and pepper, then let cool.
Mix the cooled vegetables with everything else by hand.
Pack into a 9x5-inch loaf pan lined with foil or plastic wrap and chill for several hours.
Start the smoker at 200°F, with red oak if you have it.
Turn the loaf out onto a shallow pan, put it on, and raise the heat to 300°F over about 20 minutes.
Cook until 150°F inside, about 1 to 1½ hours.
Rest for 20 minutes before slicing.

recipes.title: Egret's Cow Lickin' Chili

source.name: Egret (John Hall), Big Green Egg Forum

recipes.notes: Egret's competition chili from Eggtoberfest 2007. Steps 3 to 5 are rewritten to the big-patty house rule and keep the browned bits; tap "As written" for Egret's version. Seed the dried chiles before floating them so the seeds don't release. Cow Lick is a Dizzy Pig rub. Some versions swap the cocoa for 2 squares (1 oz each) of semi-sweet baking chocolate. Can be made on the stove too.

ingredients.item: pinto, dark kidney or black beans

steps.text: Set up the Hasty Bake or smoker at 350°F with 2 or 3 fist-sized wood chunks.
Heat the oil in the Dutch oven on the grate.
Press the chuck into the hot Dutch oven as one big patty. Sear without moving it until the bottom is deeply browned, 4 to 5 minutes. Flip and sear the second side.
steps.asWritten: Add the ground chuck and sausage, breaking them into smaller pieces with a wooden spoon.

steps.text: Break up the patty, add the sausage, close the lid and cook about 1 hour, stirring every 15 minutes.
steps.asWritten: Close the lid and cook for about 1 hour, stirring every 10 to 15 minutes.

steps.text: Lift the meat out to drain on paper towels and pour off the grease, keeping the browned bits in the pot.
steps.asWritten: Remove the meat and drain on paper towels. Wipe the Dutch oven dry with paper towels.

steps.text: Add a little more oil and sauté the onion, bell pepper, jalapeños and serranos until limp.
Add the garlic and cook 2 to 3 minutes.
Return the meat and stir in the tomatoes, Rotel, beans, spices, rub, broth and wine. Float the dried chiles on top.
Cook uncovered about 2 hours, adding water if it gets dry. Once it simmers, you can drop the heat to 300°F to 325°F.
Remove the bay leaves and dried chiles, season with salt and pepper, and serve.

recipes.title: Smoked Ribs, 2-1-1
recipes.notes: Jim's 2-1-1: 2 hours unwrapped, 1 hour wrapped, 1 hour unwrapped, then crank the heat, sauce and sear. Meathead's card is the base (rub, salt, 225°F, bend test). 2-1-1 timing fits baby backs; Meathead gives spares and St. Louis 5 to 7 hours. On the Hasty Bake, add 4 oz wood once the temp is stable and 4 oz more after 20 to 30 minutes, then no more. With a salted or bottled rub, skip the salt; store ribs labeled enhanced are already brined. Pink under the surface is smoke ring.

ingredients.note: baby back, spare or St. Louis cut
about ¼ tsp per lb; skip with a salted rub
apple, oak or hickory; Hasty Bake only

steps.text: Remove the membrane from the bone side with a butter knife and paper towel. Trim excess fat.
Optional: salt the ribs 1 to 2 hours ahead.
Wet the meat lightly and rub about 2 tbsp per side.
Set the smoker to 225°F. On the Hasty Bake, set up two-zone and add the first wood once stable.
Smoke meat side up, unwrapped, for 2 hours.
steps.asWritten: Smoke meat side up over indirect heat, lid closed, without flipping. Baby backs take 3 to 5 hours total, spares and St. Louis 5 to 7.

steps.text: Wrap tightly in foil with the water and cook 1 hour.
steps.asWritten: Optional Texas Crutch: wrap in foil with about 1 oz water for up to an hour. Meathead recommends skipping it for backyard cooking because it can soften the bark.

steps.text: Unwrap and cook 1 hour more, until the surface cracks when you bounce the slab with tongs.
Crank the heat, paint both sides with sauce and sear over the hottest spot, lid open, a minute or so per side.
steps.asWritten: Sauce only in the last 15 minutes, one light coat. For a sizzle, move over the hottest part of the grill for a minute or so per side with the lid open.

steps.text: Slice between the bones.

recipes.title: Diner Burgers (Quarter Pounders)
recipes.notes: 1 lb of beef is the four 4 oz balls the recipe yields; the source names no weight or fat ratio beyond 20 to 30% fat. Grind twice (or use the small plate) if grinding your own. Use one spatula for smashing raw meat and a clean one for flipping and serving. Meathead tops them with his burger glop, which isn't on the page; the Burger Sauce card fits. A 12-inch skillet holds 2 at a time. Nutrition is per burger.

ingredients.item: beef fat, bacon fat or vegetable oil

steps.text: Mix the pepper, onion powder and garlic powder into the beef with a fork.
Form four 2-inch balls, about 4 oz each, and refrigerate 20 minutes.
Heat the griddle as hot as it gets, at least 350°F.
Butter the buns and toast them cut side down, pressed under a plate, until golden. Wipe the griddle.
Add the fat and heat until it just starts to smoke.
Set a ball down and smash it flat right away, working the edges thin and ragged. Don't press again.
Salt the tops and leave them alone 3 to 5 minutes, until the bottoms are dark brown.
Flip with the clean spatula and press gently. Add cheese and cover to melt, about 2 minutes.
Stack on the buns with onion, lettuce and burger sauce.

recipes.title: Texas Brisket (Meathead's Original)
recipes.notes: The source your two brisket cards build on. Plan on about 1 lb raw per person. Salt is ½ tsp Morton coarse kosher per lb (2 tbsp for 12 lb); skip it if you inject or use the bottled rub. The card says 12 hours, but the article's timeline is 14 to 18 hours plus the hold. Crisp a soft bark by unwrapping and searing briefly over a hot grill or under the broiler. Burnt ends: cube the point, crisp in rendered fat, then sauce. On the pellet smoker the pellets cover the wood.

ingredients.note: optional, for injecting, about 1 oz per lb

steps.text: Trim the fat cap to ¼ inch and remove the silverskin. Note the grain direction.
Salt 12 to 24 hours ahead, or at least 2 to 4 hours before smoking.
Optional: inject about 1 oz broth per pound instead of salting.
Rub liberally and keep it chilled until it goes on.
Stabilize the smoker at 235°F, then cook at about 225°F with the water pan full.
Probe the thickest part. Add 4 oz wood as it goes on and 4 oz more over the first 2 hours.
After 3 hours, flip it if the top and bottom colors differ.
When the bark is set and it stalls at 150°F to 165°F, usually 6 to 8 hours in, wrap tight in double foil or butcher paper with the broth.
Keep cooking at 225°F. Start probing at 195°F; it's done around 203°F when the probe slides in and it wobbles.
Hold it wrapped in a cooler for 2 to 4 hours.
At the last minute, trim the ends, separate the point and flat, and slice the flat across the grain pencil-thick.
Taste the juices. Dilute with water if salty or mix with mop sauce, and serve.
